title: Verify Rework Plan
eyebrow: Build plan · #368 rework verify.py into per-part test files with a parallel runner

short.lead: This is the build plan for reworking verify.py (issue #368). It is a new step of the restructure (#306). On the proposal page you chose option 1A: split verify.py into one test file per part, with a runner that runs the parts at the same time. You also chose option 2A: during a session, the parts a change touched run twice and every other part runs once. The tests are split along the same parts as hook.py. So this rework comes after step 2 (#340), which is paused at its first part, step 2a (#357). The work is 3 sub-issues, #369 to #371. One helper agent builds each one, one at a time.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what it creates or changes and what it needs.

Step 1
List which part every check belongs to (#369)
Each of the 913 checks in verify.py is listed with its line range, what it tests, and which part it belongs to.
Checks that test two parts, and shared test setup, are listed separately.
The list goes into docs/4-systems/verify-suites.md; nothing moves yet.
Nothing from you. Done when every check is listed exactly once and the counts add up.
swap
Step 2
Per-part test files and a parallel runner (#370)
Each check moves into its part's test file; shared test setup goes into one helper module.
A runner script runs all parts at the same time by default, or only the parts a change touched.
verify.py stays as the command that runs everything, so GitHub's check and the commands in CLAUDE.md keep working.
No check is deleted: the full run must report the same number of checks.
Nothing from you. Depends on step 1.
check
Step 3
The run-twice rule, docs, timing and QA (#371)
The rule about running tests twice changes to: parts the change touched run twice, every other part runs once, and GitHub's check runs everything.
A full run and a touched-parts run are each timed and compared with the 197 seconds one full run took on 2026-10-21.
A QA page shows the before and after times.
You: answer "QA passed: verify rework" or "QA failed: verify rework".

changes: All 913 checks stay; only where they live and how they are run changes.
The full run's check count must match the count before the split, so a check that goes missing fails the step.
